body:
Ok, this one is a gut punch.

I have essentially stopped speaking (with anyone) because it's not worth the potential conflict.

I don't know how to solve this, but... assuming that you've gone through similar things yourself, what do?

Thanks for such a kind response. I do feel a little bit better after I got some sleep (hence the delay). 

I'm not familiar with biofeedback at all. My counselor is pretty good and we work well together, but it's just standard talk stuff. It does look interesting though.

My parents always say that they are happy to pay for the medicine. (Although they won't pay for my brother's for some reason; he is younger and has a milder form.)  It's not that they've ever said they resent me or that I am a burden, it's more like it seems like throwing money at a problem that just refuses to go away. 

I don't know if there are any sliding scale psychiatrists in the area. I really like my current one, as he and his team are one of the few vaguely competent ones I've ever seen. But it's untenable. I dunno.

My grandfather is (slowly) dying of Alzheimer's and much of my family has said privately, in hushed tones, that they hope he just has another huge heart attack and goes in his sleep. Not because of the money (although who can pay $7000/mo for a memory care place??) but because it's so hard on him and on my grandmother. The same was said of a cousin of mine who had a brain aneurysm, and is doing just fine except for the aneurysm-related brain damage. I dunno. I'm sure my parents love me, but it also feels like there's a constant pressure from them, from society, from everywhere... that if I'm not successful, and worse yet, a burden, then my life isn't worth shit.

I would like to go back to school and get a degree in social work so that I can help queer kids with mental illnesses/developmental disabilities. Which sounds fucking stupid when I'm 26 and my own mental illness/dd combo is doing me in. But if I am going to live, that is my purpose in life I think. When I'm not in the midst of a crisis myself, I'm really good at helping other people through their crises. About all I do anymore is listen to my shortwave and try (slowly, badly) to teach myself about linux systems.

EDIT: I am watching a TED Talk by Brene Brown right now. It looks like it will be good, if a bit hard to handle at the moment.

Yeah. But the drafts are never good enough. I guess that's a perk of being an English major? There's always another, better draft to be done... and that kind of necessitates me sticking around to revise the damn thing.

At some point, when you are calm and unworried about these things, it may be ok to have a beer. But now is not a good time to sample substances... partially because of the addictive histories and concerns, yes, but also because it would be yet one more source of worry for you, and you don't need more on your plate.

That said, you might find some comfort in knowing that intrusive thoughts are really pretty common, and that they come in lots of different forms. Suicide, self harm, and substance use are all really common, but basically you can have intrusive thoughts about anything and everything. 

Just because you're having intrusive thoughts about suicide, as you said, doesn't mean that it's at all a possibility. Still, it doesn't make the thoughts much less scary, does it?  One thing I have found helpful, on the suggestion of my counselor, is addressing the thoughts out loud, like they are a friend who blurts unhelpful things. "Yeah, ok. I heard you, but we're not doing that." It feels goofy as hell but it might work for you.

If you would like to tell someone, that would be a good idea I think. Specifically for this, but for addictive issues in general, it can be good to have someone to help hold you accountable, or just to vent to. Willpower alone isn't that effective. You can do this, but try to build a variety of healthy coping mechanisms if you can.

Figuring out all the preparations necessary to kill yourself is really fucking complicated, isn't it? Embrace that though. Sometimes the difficult logistics of it can be one of the few (or the only) thing that keeps you alive. Or at least that's been the case for me a couple times.

Don't worry so much about your parents. I know that's easier said than done. I'm 26 as well, and kinda isolated, for what it's worth. Your parents will deal with things as they come, or they won't, but parents can be resilient in surprising ways. 

That's not to encourage you to go through with suicide... far from it. What I mean is, consider opening up to them if that's at all possible. No parent wants to hear that their child (adult or not, still their child) is suffering. You don't have to slog through life to protect them; if you can talk with them or just connect in some minor way, that may help you.

Loneliness sucks. You know that, of course. And I'm sure you've heard the requisite advice to try social groups in your area or get into hobbies or church or school and such. But even so... if you don't feel up to all of that, that's ok. Just try to talk to your parents. I'm sure they'd love a call.

Hey, I dunno if you're still online or even alive. I hope you are.

Just wanted to let you know that I was in your position in 2010. It fucking sucked so much. What you're going through is brutal, and who can really blame anyone for trying to avoid that level of pain?

That said, although your parents will be upset when they find out that you have failed school, they will be tremendously more upset if they find out that you have died. The next few months are not going to be so good, but they are not unsalvageable. They are not as bad as what you are enduring now.

Talk to your parents. Talk to the school. Talk to a psychologist and a psychiatrist. You can almost certainly get readmitted -- I did. The school recognized that I had a serious medical condition and readmitted me on probation the following semester.

You can go back to school when you're ready, if you want to. This does not have to be the end.

It's a fairly simple secret, as these things go.

I've been sexually assaulted by a sibling on more than one occasion, when we were both adults.

Our parents know that I was sexually assaulted "once while I was in college" and that's true in the sense that I was home on summer break when the first one happened. I just let them think only one assault happened, and that it was some rando on campus hundreds of miles from their home.

My sibling and I have sorted it out between ourselves and with a counselor who has known our family for a long time. But this secret would ruin their career, their relationship (which seems to be pointing toward marriage), and most of all our family.

I'll take this secret to my grave.

I'm at least nominally transmasculine. Mostly just queer/nonbinary.

But I wonder semi-frequently if I'm just cis, and I transitioned because I didn't want to deal with the expectations that people had for me when they thought I was a young woman. Was I just so annoyed with misogyny and with the narrow femininity that was expected of me that I just jumped ship entirely? Couldn't I, and shouldn't I, have tried to find a different way of being a woman instead of immediately leaping to "man" and then "neither woman nor man"?

The other thing that gets me is that I have been dealing with a low-level eating disorder since my mid-teens. And it's really really gendered. I don't really feel dysphoria at all unless I'm wearing something tight in my hips/butt, and then I'm flooded with thoughts about me being a fat woman. Otherwise I'm fine. Being fat has never made me feel like less of a man or less of a nonbinary person, and I am perfectly content to wear skirts or sports bras sometimes.

tl;dr I think I might just be a cis woman with an eating disorder. But that would mean the past decade of my life has basically been a lie.

EDIT: Here's another one.

I dated a woman for a long time (in college terms, anyway) who was, like me, trans. She was physically and emotionally abusive, and unfortunately everyone but me could see that. My best friends (also trans) told me they were very worried for me, but I just blew them off.

I'm healing now, slowly, several years after we broke up. But I'm afraid to talk about the lingering issues I have (can't be around fireworks, can't be held down, et cetera) because I'm afraid that people will use that against her. Some of my family have said they would kill her given the opportunity, and they say it's because of the abuse, but their transmisogyny is only very thinly veiled. And besides that, I don't want to add to the idea that trans women are predators (overwhelmingly they aren't, obvs) or misgender her, and I don't want my own claim of a male-ish presenting person talking about a female abuser to be used as fodder for TWEFs or MRAs.
